programmes.cash: None. Explicitly no capital, no fees, no dues.
programmes.terms_dilution: Zero equity. SPC blog: "There is no cost, no right to invest, and no requirement that you're starting a company." The SPC Fund has no right to invest in anything you start.
programmes.cohort_dates: 6-month residency, rolling start
programmes.location_requirement: Must be located in and physically attend SF, NYC or Bangalore. FAQ: "Members are expected to come into SPC throughout the week, which usually means that folks need to be located in SF, NYC, or Bangalore."
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Solo-friendly. Explicitly for individual technologists; co-founders apply separately. Many members find co-founders inside the community.
programmes.network_quality: ~175 active members, 1300+ alumni. Very high technical density.
programmes.customer_access: Peer/technologist network rather than customer pipeline. Forums on frontier topics.
programmes.brand_value: High - SPC is a recognised -1 to 0 institution.
programmes.application_effort: ~2-3 hours; written application then interview if shortlisted. No video required per published process.
programmes.notes: THIS IS A DIFFERENT PROGRAMME from the SPC Founder Fellowship (filed 2026-07-31, rejected 2026-08-11). The Member Residency is the equity-free exploratory track with rolling admissions, a separate application path, and a Bangalore hub - the founder is already in Bangalore. FAQ note: "If you're planning to fundraise soon, we may instead ask you to apply for our Founder Fellowship." Supaprod being product-complete may push the reviewer back toward the Fellowship track; worth framing as -1 to 0 on go-to-market rather than product. SPC India also runs a frontier-problems framing at southparkcommons.com/india/. Prior rejection on the Fellowship is a real headwind and needs a judgement call before filing.

programmes.credits_and_tools: >$800k in partner perks (AWS, Stripe, Mercury, Carta).

programmes.notes: Same organisation also links the Solo Founders Program (separate row). ODF is pure network value: no cheque, ~$1000 cost, 36-hour decision - cheap to test. The page states applicants should not have already raised beyond pre-seed or found product-market fit; Supaprod is pre-revenue with zero external users, so this fits cleanly.

programmes.name: Solo Founders Program (SFP) - Fall 2026
programmes.page_evidence: solofounders.com/program: "Apply by Sept 2026" and "Applications reviewed on a rolling basis." LinkedIn 2026-07-28: "Applications are now open for the Solo Founders Program." Verified by direct fetch 2026-08-14.

programmes.solo_founder_stance: Purpose-built for solo founders - this is the entire thesis. "If you're already solo, you're early."

programmes.brand_value: Rising. Small but sharply positioned; the solo-founder framing is a direct match.

programmes.notes: Strongest structural fit in this lane: the one programme where being a solo founder is the qualification rather than the objection. Requires 3 months physically in SF from 2026-09-10, which collides directly with the mid-September public launch - that clash is the decision to make. Explicitly accepts founders who have already gone through another accelerator or raised: "SFP is designed to layer on top of whatever path you're already taking, not force you to choose between us and your next round."

programmes.location_requirement: One week in person in Silicon Valley
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No stated preference for teams. "You can fill out just one application for your team. If you have a co-founder, make sure to note this somewhere." Individuals routinely accepted.

programmes.notes: Effectively free optionality: no deadline, no equity required, one week of commitment. Explicitly no age restriction ("technical builders of all ages"), no company required, no need to quit your job. The ten short essays are the whole application - a writing exercise the founder-answer-playbook material maps onto directly.

programmes.name: Entrepreneur First - Bangalore Program
programmes.page_evidence: apply.joinef.com lists live programmes with apply buttons including a Bangalore Program. EF FAQ: "If you're based in India, you can apply for our Bangalore programs" and "We accept applications on a rolling basis and review each one carefully."
programmes.cash: Location-specific. The published US structure is up to $250K ($125K post-money SAFE for 8% plus $125K uncapped MFN SAFE).
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity taken. US terms published as ~8% for the first tranche. Bangalore terms follow analogous structures with location-specific entities and are NOT published - must confirm.
programmes.cohort_dates: FORM: 12-14 weeks in the Bangalore office. LAUNCH: teams that receive Investment Committee funding relocate to San Francisco for the final ~12 weeks.
programmes.location_requirement: Full-time, in-person in Bangalore for FORM, then SF for LAUNCH. Founder is already in Bangalore - no relocation needed for phase one.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly solo-first. "No you do not need a cofounder to apply. Our program brings together exceptional individuals to find a cofounder and build a startup from scratch. We assess all applicants as individuals."
programmes.network_quality: Very high. Portfolio value $16B+, backed by Sequoia, a16z, SoftBank, Khosla.
programmes.customer_access: Structured GTM support during LAUNCH; not a corporate customer pipeline.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Shared office space in the local hub plus SF; perks not itemised publicly.
programmes.brand_value: High, especially in Europe and India.
programmes.application_effort: ~3-5 hours plus three interview rounds. Apply to only ONE programme in ONE hub city at a time - this is an explicit EF rule.
programmes.notes: EF's core mechanic is co-founder matching, which cuts both ways: it is the most solo-friendly programme on this list, but it wants you pre-idea and Supaprod is a shipped product with 5,172 commits. The counter-framing is that EF backs the individual, and a founder who shipped a full lifecycle OS solo is exactly that profile. The one-programme-at-a-time rule forces a choice between Bangalore, London XF2, the Bridge Residency and the US track. Note EF incorporates a Delaware C-Corp during the programme on the US pathway, which suits the founder's structure preference.
